items.title: AISI 红队论文：攻击策略选择会让 LLM 监视器评估结果失真
items.description: 英国 AI Security Institute 发布论文，测试合成攻击生成方式对监视器评估的影响。评估一个 OpenAI 前生产监视器时，同一监视器对不同攻击策略的漏报率从 0.2%（基础提示）到 23%（转录编辑）不等，优化程度也会显著改变结果。作者指出合成转录只是真实有害行为代理，其代表性难以证明，仅凭监视器评估不足以保证部署安全，需辅以能力限制、人工在环和沙箱等分层防护。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/tl8v9gto8rd3e4x40xfbljj13
items.author: noreply@aihot.news (英国 AI Security Institute：Blog)

items.title: Anthropic 访谈 58 家企业客户：AI 采用的价值、雇佣影响与组织重组
items.description: Anthropic 研究团队对 58 家企业客户进行 66 次面对面访谈，分析企业采用 AI 的方式、瓶颈与组织变化。研究发现多数 AI 应用通过扩大产出而非削减成本创造价值；直接裁员案例很少，但约三分之二的公司因 AI 减少招聘，九家削减外包和离岸承包商；高价值应用通常需要更深度的组织重组，如拓宽岗位职责、把员工转向 AI 无法完成的瓶颈任务，以及为非技术员工建设数据和基础设施支持。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/gj8mzwrgqlkvim6xe382a35q2
items.author: noreply@aihot.news (Anthropic：Research)

items.title: 用户实测用 MiniCPM5-2B 在 Mac 上本地跑通体检报告分析
items.description: 用户@cxjwin 分享在 Mac（M4 Pro、48GB）上用 Homebrew 装 llama.cpp 跑 minicpm5-2b、colima 起 Docker 本地运行开源项目 Mirobody 的实测：14 页 PDF 首次处理漏掉 3 页扫描版化验单，截图单独上传后 58 行化验数值逐项与原件对上，其中 20 行成功映射到 LOINC 标准编码，肌酐因名称歧义留空未猜。问超标指标时 2B 模型走 11 步找到全部 5 项箭头指标，但把一项在范围内的血糖误判为超标。接 Claude Code 时改用演示账号避免数据上传。Mirobody 由 Theta Health 以 Apache-2.0 开源，网页版和微信小程序也基于它。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/g3vdho0vzm8rzriiz5grruy3m

items.author: 山宗
items.content: 过去几天，围绕 Claude 参与证明黎曼猜想的讨论，几乎席卷了整个科技圈和数学界。其中最令人津津乐道的一个细节，是这份证明如果翻译成人类能够阅读的文字，篇幅将超过 25 万页。 就在刚刚，Anthropic 数学家 Levent Alpöge 在社交平台 X 上发布长文，回应过去几天围绕黎曼猜想证明产生的诸多争议，并逐一反思自己在成果发布过程中犯下的错误。 Alpöge 表示，他原本以为自己在主定理中刻意繁琐地描述实数全序关系，已经足以让人意识到其中的幽默成分，没想到外界真的把这个数字当成了事实，并广泛传播。需要重点明确的是，Alpöge 此次回应并未否定黎曼猜想证明的有效性，他承认的错误主要涉及成果发布时的不当表述，以及形式化证明代码中存在的大量冗余。 由于成果公布后的几天里，他并不想在社交媒体上发言，因此也没有及时澄清，不过倒是看了不少网友制作的表情包。「陶哲轩建议不要在论文里开玩笑，现在我终于明白为什么了。」 按照此前披露的信息，整个研究项目于 10 月 6 日启动，历时约 41 天。Alpöge 与 Claude 在 11 月 15 日完成核心证明的最后一步，随后于 11 月 16 日将研究成果扩展至广义黎曼猜想。 与传统数学研究成果的发布方式不同，Alpöge 没有提供一篇完整的自然语言论文，而是公开了一份仅有 4 页的说明文档，以及一套规模惊人的 Lean 形式化证明代码。

items.author: 山宗
items.content: 就在刚刚，Lean 和 Mathlib 社区发布联合声明，宣布正式认证 Anthropic 数学家 Levent Alpöge 提交的黎曼猜想形式化证明，并表示对其正确性具有充分信心。 更引人关注的是，Alpöge 此前透露，这项研究由他与 AI 模型 Claude 合作完成。在证明接近终点时，Claude 展现出的数学推理能力，甚至超出了他的预期。 11 月 20 日，Alpöge 在个人网站公布研究成果，宣称解决了著名的黎曼猜想（Riemann Hypothesis），同时取得了涉及广义黎曼猜想（Generalized Riemann Hypothesis）的结果。 它涉及黎曼 ζ 函数非平凡零点的分布，核心命题是所有非平凡零点的实部是否都等于 1/2。由于这一问题与素数分布密切相关，过去一个多世纪，无数数学家尝试攻克，却始终未能找到严格证明。 马斯克也发文感叹，证明黎曼猜想能够让大量此前依赖该猜想成立的数学结论摆脱条件限制，成为无条件成立的定理，并称其为超级智能取得的又一项惊人成就。 他曾尝试让 Claude 将证明整理成人类能够阅读的文字版本，结果生成的草稿超过 25 万页，庞大到连他本人都认为难以阅读。如此惊人的篇幅，甚至被部分网友戏称为一场针对数学界的「DDoS 攻击」。

items.author: Sarah Perez
items.content: Anthropic is moving from having Claude write code to helping developers decide when that code is ready to ship. On Monday, the newly public AI company announced the launch of Claude Ship , a suite of AI agents for automating code reviews, fixes, and approvals of routine code changes. The latter is the more interesting part of this new set of tools, as AI coding tools already offered code review features before now. What’s notable about Claude Ship is not just that it can review proposed code changes and identify and address problems, but that it also includes an agent that can approve code changes automatically based on policies set by a development team. The launch arrives at a time when AI coding agents have become increasingly capable of generating substantial amounts of code, leading to bottlenecks in reviewing and approving the code changes before they go live. With Claude Ship, the idea is to automate even more of the work involved in the development process, essentially by delegating approval authority to an AI agent itself. “Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” a company blog post explains. “On the Claude Code team, Claude writes most of our code, and we wanted everything after the PR to move that fast too.” Claude Ship is launching in beta, allowing early adopters to use it to review pull requests (PRs), and then decide what’s ready to merge. items.title: Elon Musk and others rejoice as Jensen Huang is reinstated at Nvidia amid scandal
items.description: "The mistake has been corrected," Elon Musk chimed in.
items.author: Amanda Silberling
items.content: A handful of tech CEOs, including Elon Musk, are celebrating Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia. Despite being caught in three affairs — including one with an alleged Chinese spy that has triggered multiple congressional investigations over national security concerns — Huang was reinstated as CEO and president of Nvidia on Monday morning. “The mistake has been corrected,” Tesla and SpaceX leader Elon Musk wrote on X about Huang’s return. Musk had been among the most vocal tech leaders to advocate for Huang. “I think it’s like kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak, and it just doesn’t seem like a good thing for shareholders,” Musk said last week at the DealBook Summit. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman had taken a more neutral stance, commenting last week, “It’s hard to imagine the AI industry without Jensen.” Altman had experienced a similar situation when he was ousted as CEO of OpenAI, then reinstated days later. After the announcement that Huang would return, Altman simply posted, “Jensen!” Many other tech CEOs have similarly refrained from commenting on the matter, given the shifting politics surrounding Huang’s ouster and reinstatement, as well as the national security concerns at the center of the controversy.

The company will be added to the Commerce Department’s Entity List, the outlet writes. This list “contains the names of foreign parties” subject to certain export restrictions designed to ensure that “sensitive technologies do not fall into the hands of those who would threaten U.S. national security or American citizens.” Functionally, what this will mean is that U.S. companies will not be able to do business with or sell products to Megaspeed without first gaining a special license from the federal government. Semafor cites anonymous sources familiar with the matter to note the move is designed to stop the company “from obtaining US-made semiconductors.” Megaspeed is a Singapore-based cloud and AI infrastructure provider that, during the period that Nvidia’s boss, Jensen Huang, self-admittedly had an affair with Huang, was one of Nvidia’s biggest chip customers. Last week, the Commerce Department also announced it had launched a criminal probe into the company. Authorities in both the U.S. and Singapore are now probing whether the company defied export restrictions and illegally smuggled Nvidia chips to China . The company has denied wrongdoing. items.title: Nvidia employees greet Jensen Huang like a hero as he returns to company’s HQ
items.description: "I'm going to be a better CEO the second time around," Huang told employees.
items.author: Amanda Silberling
items.content: Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia’s offices on Monday to an applauding crowd of hundreds of employees, according to several videos circulating online. The embattled Nvidia founder had stepped down earlier this month amid a series of scandals — including an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, which has triggered multiple Congressional hearings over national security, and two affairs with Nvidia employees — but was reinstated as CEO after pushback from the tech community and an intervention by President Donald Trump. After basking in chants of his name, Huang briefly addressed the crowd. “Thank you all for the second chance,” he said. “I’m going to be a better CEO the second time around.” Over 200,000 people, including around 10,000 current Nvidia employees, had signed an open letter advocating for Huang’s return. Other tech leaders also pushed for Huang’s reinstatement, including Elon Musk, who said last week at the DealBook Summit that letting Huang go is like “kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak.” Amid this increased scrutiny, however, other reports have depicted a different side to Nvidia’s top exec — one where Jensen is not seen as a beloved leader, but as a brutal bully. Based on decades of court documents and over a dozen interviews with current and former Nvidia employees, The New York Times reported that Huang “used humiliation as a tool” and verbally belittled staff at times.

items.title: Amazon snaps up Decart’s AI optimization tech for $7.5B as it prepares to sell Trainium chips
items.description: Amazon is acquiring Decart’s AI optimization technology and research team in a reported $7.5 billion deal.
items.author: Rebecca Bellan
items.content: Amazon has agreed to acquire a good chunk of Israeli startup Decart. The e-commerce and cloud giant is paying $7.5 billion for the startup, according to Bloomberg. Decart has made a name for itself building interactive real-time world models — most recently Oasis 3 — and AI video-generation tools. But under the hood, the company stands out for its Decart Optimization Stack (DOS), software that helps AI models run efficiently on Nvidia, Amazon, and Google’s hardware. As part of the deal, Amazon will acquire the technology behind DOS, as well as Decart’s founding team and team of AI researchers and engineers, Amazon said in a blog post . “Every leap forward in AI starts with getting more out of every chip,” said Peter DeSantis, SVP of foundational AI models, custom silicon, quantum computing, at Amazon. “More efficient compute means better training, better reinforcement learning, faster inference, and better models for customers at a lower cost.” Amazon, which has so far been using its Trainium chips at its own data centers, is preparing to start selling them to customers as a competitor to Nvidia. Decart’s technology could make it easier for customers to run their workloads on Amazon chips, rather than Nvidia’s, which has been the gold standard so far.

items.title: Jensen Huang isn’t out of the woods yet

With so much of the AI industry built on top of Nvidia’s AI infrastructure, Huang’s departure looked like an imminent threat to the business — and the mood on his return has been ecstatic. Share prices are rocketing back up, particularly for neoclouds like CoreWeave and Nebius, and the Nasdaq rose 7% on the news. Still, tech leaders should be clear-eyed about all the problems likely to come with Huang’s reinstatement. President Trump is already telling reporters that the U.S. government found no national security concerns resulting from the affair, but the broader national security concerns aren’t so easy to dismiss, and Trump’s involvement may do more harm than good for Nvidia and its partners. This isn’t the end of the problems caused by Huang’s affairs; it’s likely just the beginning. items.content: Enterprise customer experience company Sierra , co-founded by former Salesforce co-CEO Bret Taylor, said on Monday that it has raised $1.75 billion in a Series F round that doubles the company’s valuation to $30 billion. The new raise comes within six months of its previous round, which valued the company at $15 billion . The new round was led by Greenoaks and Lightspeed Venture Partners, with participation from existing investors who have led previous rounds, including Benchmark, Sequoia, Greenoaks, GV, and Tiger Global. Enterprise automation is among the few areas where AI has seen rapid adoption. Sierra said that it currently serves almost 50% of Fortune 50 companies, and its clients include BNY, HSBC, Singtel, Wells Fargo, JPMorganChase, Pearson, Next, and Cox Automotive. The company late last month said its outcome-based pricing model has helped it double its run-rate revenue to $400 million within five months . That said, Sierra is working along similar lines as other customer experience players in the market, which is creating a platform to build agents and partner with model developers to provide choices to enterprises. As personal and work agents interact with enterprise systems, Sierra is also working on creating protocol definitions for agents with companies like Meta, Stripe, and Walmart. items.title: Nvidia reverses course and brings Jensen Huang back as CEO
items.description: The stunning reversal was supported by senior officials in the U.S. government.
items.author: Kirsten Korosec
items.content: In a stunning reversal, Nvidia’s board said on Monday that it had reinstated Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO and president, less than two weeks after he resigned following his admission of at least two extramarital affairs, one of which was with a woman whom the U.S. government suspects to be a Chinese spy. The decision marks an extraordinary comeback for one of the tech industry’s most influential executives, whose abrupt departure raised questions about national security and the future of the world’s most valuable chipmaker. Notably, the U.S. government itself played a role in his return: Nvidia’s board said it consulted senior government officials before determining that Huang posed no national security risk. Nvidia shares, which had already shot up in premarket trading, opened 30% higher. Nvidia shares were priced at $159.95 a share, up 27%, at 9:51 a.m. ET. In the days since Huang resigned, President Donald Trump has repeatedly expressed his support for the ousted executive, who is now back at the helm of the AI chip giant. Trump said in a post on Truth Social that the board “made the correct and proper decision to return” Huang to the position, noting that the U.S. government has no reason to believe that Nvidia poses any risk to national security. Trump also said the U.S. attorney general confirmed that the U.S. government doesn’t have any evidence that Huang engaged in any illegal activity. items.title: How Notable Capital, GIC, and Baillie Gifford bet big on Anthropic before its IPO
items.description: Three significant backers share what gave them conviction to bet billions on Anthropic.
items.author: Marina Temkin
items.content: When Notable Capital poured roughly 10% of the U.S. portion of its $1 billion-plus fund into Anthropic’s Series E, many limited partners were perplexed by the massive bet. Claude’s maker was still trailing its biggest rival, OpenAI, and DeepSeek had released its R1 model just weeks earlier, threatening to overtake closed-source competitors. Moreover, at $61.5 billion, Anthropic’s valuation was by far the highest that the predominantly early-stage venture firm had invested at in its 25-year history. But investors at Notable, formerly known as GGV Capital before its 2024 split from its China operations, were confident in Anthropic’s future. A team that included managing partners Hans Tung and Glenn Solomon and principal Dan Cahana crunched the numbers and found that developers were increasingly favoring Claude over ChatGPT, using Claude 70% of the time, a reversal from the previous year. “We just knew that for AI, the developer is at the center because they’re the early adopters,” Tung, a co-founder of the firm, told TechCrunch. Having navigated the complexities of U.S.-China relations firsthand, Notable was also convinced that “mission-critical” work would always require U.S.-based, closed-source models, Tung said. Less than two years later, Notable’s LPs are no longer questioning the outsized investment.
